findings.text: Privileged restart control entry validates boot capability in the caller pid namespace and a magic pair, gives child pid namespaces to a dedicated handler, then dispatches restart, CAD flag changes, halt, power off, restart with user argument, and optional kexec or suspend requests.

Power off without power off capability is rewritten to halt with a fallback marker set. Halt and power off paths terminate the caller rather than returning normally. The restart with argument variant bounds the user string. Unrecognized commands are rejected.
The restart control entry holds a global system transition mutex across the whole command dispatch and releases it only on paths that return normally.
The CAD entry point selects between scheduling deferred restart work when the CAD flag is enabled and signaling the configured CAD pid otherwise.
CAD and pid signal helpers deliver a signal to a pid object through the thread group signal path, with CAD delivery resolving a globally held pid under read side protection.
Pid signal delivery retries when the target lookup races with unhashing or thread group leader changes, returning only once a stable target is signaled or absence is confirmed.
CAD pid dereference and pid to task resolution occur under read side RCU protection, with unlock before returning the delivery result.

Orderly reboot and power off are deferred to workqueue helpers that invoke configured user helpers and, on failure, can fall back to emergency synchronization plus a forced kernel restart or power off.
The forced power off marker is sticky once set and is not cleared by later non forced requests, so a pending forced shutdown dominates.

Hardware protection trigger runs once per boot, records the selected action, arms a delayed forced fallback, then starts an orderly reboot or forced orderly shutdown. The delayed worker forces the recorded action and finally attempts emergency restart.

Hardware protection configuration accepts two named actions and reports an undefined label for other values. A default placeholder is replaced by the configured global action at trigger time. Stores require administrator capability.
Power off helper path storage limit is 256 bytes and the compiled in defaults name system power off and reboot helpers.

Early reboot option parsing consumes comma separated tokens selecting warm, cold, hard, soft, or gpio modes, single letter type codes, a force flag, and an optional reboot cpu with range validation, disabling automatic defaults whenever any token is present.

Reboot mode, type, force, and cpu sysfs controls render current settings on read and on write require boot capability, validate enumerated names or numeric ranges, clear the default marker, and reject unknown inputs.

Reboot sysfs vocabulary distinguishes mode labels for cold, warm, hard, soft, gpio, and undefined, and type labels for triple, keyboard, bios, acpi, efi, and pci, exposed under mode, force, type, cpu, and hardware protection attributes.
CAD pid control reads the current numeric pid under protection and on write resolves the requested pid, exchanges the global reference, waits for existing readers, then releases the old reference.
Kernel reboot sysctls expose power off command string, CAD enable integer, and CAD pid integer with distinct access modes and dedicated handlers.

Relay mmap support validates that the requested mapping length matches the channel allocation, binds the buffer to the mapping with expansion disabled, and resolves faults to the backing vmalloc pages.

Relay buffer storage is a page array of zeroed pages mapped as one vmalloc region with per page back linkage, rounded up to page granularity, with full cleanup of allocated pages and the array on partial failure.

Relay channel and buffer lifetime uses reference counts where creation holds the channel, destruction unmaps the region, frees pages, clears the per cpu slot, and releases the channel, with a dedicated callback for buffer release.

Observed relay objects link a channel holding subbuffer counts, allocation size, base name, parent, callbacks, and per cpu buffer pointers to buffers holding start address, page array and count, padding, produced and consumed counters, offsets, wait state, and statistics.

Relay fullness and emptiness derive from produced minus consumed subbuffers relative to the channel subbuffer count, with full transitions counted and an optional channel start callback able to influence acceptance.

Global relay reset serializes iteration over possible cpu buffers with a dedicated channels mutex, while single global channel reset bypasses that lock; per buffer reset synchronizes pending wakeup work before clearing counters.
Relay buffer files are named by appending the cpu number to the channel base name, with creation failures normalized to absence, and buffer dentries record early byte size at association time.

Halt and power off dispatch terminate the caller without releasing the global transition lock, so those paths never reach the normal unlock and halt can fall through toward power off if the halt primitive returns.
Relay fault handling reports allocation failure when no buffer is bound and bus error when the backing page cannot be resolved, rather than succeeding with an empty page.
